newsitem.title: UK: Britain protests as Nigeria holds detainee.
newsitem.headline: Britain protests as Nigeria holds detainee.

text.p: The British Foreign Office said a Briton held without charge in Nigeria for the past two months will not be freed on Friday as had been hoped.
Nigerian acting High Commissioner (ambassador) Uche Okeke was called into the Foreign Office to hear a strong protest at the continued detention of Bruce Henderson, a Foreign Office spokesman said.
"We are extremely disappointed," the spokesman said. "We protested vigorously to the acting High Commissioner"
Britain expected Nigeria to honour a commitment to free Henderson without delay. The Foreign Office was considering what action to take next, but the spokesman gave no details.

Henderson, 42, was detained on December 22 while travelling in the politically sensitive Bakassi peninsula in southeast Nigeria where troops from Nigeria and Cameroon have frequently clashed over their rival territorial claims to the oil-rich area.
The British High Commission in Lagos, which only heard about Henderson's detention on January 8, had said earlier there were indications that he might be freed "sooner rather than later".
Henderson, from Aberdeenshire, was working on a rain forest project in Cameroon. He is said to be safe and well and now being held in Lagos.

Military-ruled Nigeria is shunned internationally for alleged human rights violations involving the detention of many opposition figures, including Moshood Abiola, the presumed winner of an annulled 1993 presidential election.
No comment was available from the Nigerian High Commission in London.
